Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 93, English)
Solar Panels, the Repair & Maintenance Fund, and the Teaching on the Gr eat Subtle Body (Maha Sookshm Sharir)

This session opens mid-conversation with a practical discussion about an inverter fuse failur e and electricity infrastructur e during Mahotsav , which develops into a discussion about installing solar panels and starting a formal r epair -and-maintenance fund, and then flows into an extended personal teaching fr om the speaker on why he never asks devotees for anything, framed ar ound the concept of a shar ed "Maha Sookshm Sharir" (Gr eat Subtle Body) connecting Ashaeiynn's community . This session has substantial live back-and-forth thr oughout (infrastructur e troubleshooting, financial suggestions, and dir ect dialogue with attendees), so it is pr esented as a full 3-part document.

1. Opening Technical Issue: An Inverter Fuse Failur e During Mahotsav The session opens with a practical discussion about the venue's inverter fuse having blown, leading to a debate about whether to bypass the inverter and run lights directly of f the generator instead, with concern raised that overuse of inverter -powered lighting (left on carelessly by attendees) may be straining the system and driving up costs.

2. Suggestion: Move to Dir ect Generator Connections and Reduce Uncontr olled Inverter Use The speaker and attendees discuss disconnecting the inverter circuit entirely and wiring lights directly to the generator , with the practical reasoning that continuing to run everything through the inverter risks burning it out entirely .

3. Pr oposal: Install Solar Panels at Ashaeiynn A devotee proposes installing solar panels, noting that Hanuman ji Maharaj's guru could "send full ener gy" to Ashaeiynn through such means; the group discusses practicality — using the rooftop area (currently reserved for deepdaan, lamp-of fering) by raising the panel structure on a shed so the space below remains usable, citing examples of other ashrams doing the same.

4. Practical Solar Discussion: Costs, Subsidy , and Bill Reduction Attendees discuss that government subsidies are available for solar installation, that installing panels typically halves or more of an electricity bill, and that excess power generated can even be sold back to the grid — with one attendee sharing that their own electricity bill dropped from roughly ₹89,000 to just ₹400–500 after installing a partial system.

5. Light Moment: A Joking Accusation of "Commission" When a devotee volunteers to look into solar panel vendors on Bhaiya's behalf, another jokes that she must have a commission arrangement with a solar company — a light, humorous exchange before the group returns to Jai Siyaram chanting.

6. Teaching: All of This Year's Resour ces Are Directed to the Havan The speaker clarifies that whatever Ashaeiynn has earned this year is being directed, as fully as possible, toward the ongoing Mahotsav havan (fire ritual) rather than infrastructure improvements like fans or comfort upgrades — framing devotion to the havan as his first priority .

7. Endorsement: Starting a Formal Repair & Maintenance Fund The speaker agrees with a suggestion (drawing on the Jain community's temple-maintenance tradition of a "sarv sadharan fund," a general fund for repairs) that Ashaeiynn should start its own
repair -and-maintenance fund, acknowledging this is necessary and that he intends to act on it, ideally starting from this Mahotsav onward, with contributions scaled to what each person can give.

8. Discussion: Fund Structur e — Foundation Pr eferred Over Trust The group briefly discusses legal structuring for such a fund, with a devotee suggesting a foundation structure is more favorable than a trust for this purpose, and the speaker deferring to others' expertise on the specific legal bylaws while af firming the underlying need for the fund.

9. Teaching: Baba Pr ovides Exactly What Is Needed for the Havan — No Mor e, No Less The speaker shares that in his experience, the funds available to him genuinely match what is needed for the havan almost exactly; if that money were diverted elsewhere, there would be no separate source to cover the havan's needs — comparing this to a father giving pocket money for a specific purpose: however it's spent, it still counts against that same original amount.

10. Disclosur e: This Year's Rising Costs for Gola (Havan Offering Balls) and Ghee The speaker discloses that the price of "gola" (a havan of fering material) has risen to over ₹400/kg this year — roughly two and a half times more expensive than before — and that Baba's instruction this year calls for a substantially lar ger quantity of ghee (a minimum of over 10,500 kg), leading Ashaeiynn to source gola from Sri Lanka and Thailand due to steep domestic price increases.

1 1. Vow: The Havan Must Never Be Allowed to Run Short The speaker states a personal vow that the havan of ferings — sourced from money he considers earmarked specifically by Baba for that purpose — must never run short, even if it means going without other comforts (like fans) himself.

12. Teaching: Why the Speaker Never Personally Asks Devotees for Money The speaker explains that he has never , in his life, asked another person directly for money — he only "asks" his deity/guru, and receives what's needed through devotees' own free will and inspiration, without solicitation.

13. Teaching: Devotees Are Never Restricted or Questioned on How They Use Communal Resour ces The speaker shares that he never restrains the younger caretakers ("bachche") who run the ashram day-to-day from using electricity or resources as they see fit, even when costs run high — reasoning that if their due share is denied, the underlying spiritual account remains "incomplete" and inevitably cycles back to af fect him anyway , since they are all part of the same interconnected subtle body .

14. Teaching: The Concept of the Maha Sookshm Sharir (Great Subtle Body) The speaker introduces the central teaching of this session: all of Ashaeiynn's members are considered part of one shared "Maha Sookshm Sharir" (Great Subtle Body), with Parikshit Bhaiya as its master (swami) and Hanuman ji Maharaj as its guru — meaning what benefits or harms any one member spiritually reverberates through the whole connected group.

15. Teaching: Giving and Receiving Within a Connected Subtle Body Is Not "T aking" The speaker teaches that because devotees' subtle bodies are interconnected, if he gives something to a devotee, he will in turn receive something back from that same connection — this is described as the natural order ("niyati") of the subtle world, not a transactional exchange.

16. Warning: Misusing or "Stealing" Within the Connected Subtle Body Causes Real Loss to Oneself The speaker warns that if members exploit or take advantage of each other within this connected subtle body (e.g. quietly pocketing money that isn't rightfully theirs), the resulting loss inevitably returns to the taker — because they are drawing from a shared, interconnected resource, not an external one.

17. Teaching: Interfering With the Great Subtle Body Extends One's Own Karmic Cycle The speaker teaches that if a person disturbs or interferes with an element of the Maha Sookshm Sharir that connects to another universe/dimension's ener gy , the return cycle for that ener gy takes longer ("cycle aur tenure badh jaata hai") before it eventually comes back around.

18. Illustration: What Five Days Without Havan Would Cost the Community The speaker of fers a vivid hypothetical: if the havan were to stop for even five days, many people's lives would be af fected — astral attacks, increased vulnerability to tantrik practices and pitru (ancestral spirit) attacks, disrupted access to Baba's protective power — illustrating why he treats the havan's continuity as nonnegotiable regardless of personal cost.

19. Illustration: Ankur Bhaiya's Injury and the Community's Shar ed Emotional Response The speaker cites the community's collective distress when a member , Ankur Bhaiya, was injured, as a real-world example of how tightly the group's subtle bodies are emotionally bonded — describing this same bond as the reason good news (like a newly-opened spiritual "drishti") brings collective joy even to those it doesn't directly af fect.

20. Personal Story: Recognizing a Karmic Debt Behind a Lie The speaker recounts a time someone came to him with what he immediately sensed was a fabricated story of hardship, provoking anger and an impulse to send the person away — until Baba revealed to him that he personally owed that individual a karmic debt from a past connection, which reframed his response entirely into patience and continued support, since the debt still needed to be resolved.

21. Teaching: "Guru Ka Guru Kaun? Guru Wahi Jo Satya Bata De" (Who Is the Guru's Guru? The One Who Reveals the Truth) Continuing the debt story , the speaker credits his own guru's guidance (via Baba's revelation) with helping him see the deeper truth behind a frustrating situation, reframing anger into patience.

22. Teaching: "Jagat Sath Ho Aur Jagdish Rooth Jaaye" — Divine Favor Outweighs Worldly Favor The speaker shares the teaching that if the whole world supports you but God (Jagdish) is displeased, nothing can save you; but if the whole world opposes you while God is on your side, no harm can touch you.

23. Teaching: One Only Asks From the Guru — Never From "One's Own People" The speaker restates his core philosophy: one should never ask anything of one's own people (apne), since things are naturally given to family , not taken from them; if anything is to be asked for , it should be asked only of God/Guru.

24. Devotee Suggestion: Add a Payment Wallet and Optional Donation Featur e to the Ashaeiynn App A devotee proposes adding a personal payment "wallet" feature to the Ashaeiynn app (so members can save funds toward their own havan/ahuti costs at their own pace) alongside a separate, entirely optional donation feature for those who wish to contribute toward the community's general needs — explicitly framed as voluntary and not something anyone would be pressured into. The speaker welcomes the suggestion and commits to considering it.

25. Teaching: "Nange Aaye The, Nange Chale Jaoge" (Y ou Came With Nothing, You Will Leave With Nothing) — With a Lighthearted Exception The speaker closes with the traditional teaching that nothing material can be carried beyond this life — followed immediately by a playful joke that the one exception might be "Dinesh ji's samosa," drawing laughter from the group.

26. Closing Teaching: Destiny Rewards Good Intent, and Devotion Should Not Waver With Circumstance The speaker closes by teaching that destiny provides according to the sincerity of one's intent (niyat), and encourages continued, unwavering Jai Siyaram jaap — cautioning against switching mantras, tantras, or yantras with changing circumstances, since consistent, singular faith is what allowed Jai Siyaram's power to be demonstrated even when the wider world doubted it.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session begins with practical infrastructure discussion (inverter/generator troubleshooting, a proposal to install solar panels) before developing into a broader teaching on community finances and interconnectedness; it is a full 3-part document given its extensive live back-and-forth. Ashaeiynn intends to start a formal repair -and-maintenance fund (modeled on Jain temple tradition), with contributions scaled to what each person can give and no one pressured to contribute. All of this year's available resources are being prioritized for the ongoing Mahotsav havan; rising costs for gola and ghee this year have required sourcing materials internationally . The speaker states he never personally asks devotees for money — funds are only ever "asked" of the guru/deity , and provided through devotees' free will and inspiration.

Central teaching: Ashaeiynn's members are described as part of one connected "Maha Sookshm Sharir" (Great Subtle Body), with Parikshit Bhaiya as swami and Hanuman ji Maharaj as guru — meaning benefit or harm to any one member spiritually reverberates through the whole group, and resources used within this connection are never simply "taken," only ever cycled and eventually returned. A devotee proposed adding an optional payment wallet and donation feature to the Ashaeiynn app; the speaker welcomed the idea as a way to let members contribute at their own convenience without solicitation. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 93, Hinglish)
Solar Panels, the Repair & Maintenance Fund, and the Teaching on the Gr eat Subtle Body (Maha Sookshm Sharir)

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept.
Exchange 1 — The Solar Panel Discussion

Devotee: Bhaiya, Hanuman ji Maharaj ke Guru ji khud Ashaeiynn ko poori urja bhejenge — solar lagwa lijiye. Bhaiya: Arre bahen, udhar hi bhej do haath se. Devotee: Bhaiya, humne kai ashramon mein dekha hai aisa — solar structure oopar khada ho jaata hai, neeche ka area deepdaan ke liye use ho sakta hai side se khula rahega. Bhaiya: Sahi hai, jagah toh hai, poora lag jayega. Devotee: Bhaiya hamara 89,000 bill aata tha, ab ₹400-500 hi aata hai — sirf teen panels lagwane se itna fark ho gaya.

Why this is her e: A concr ete, practical exchange with r eal numbers that other users may find genuinely useful if they'r e considering similar infrastructur e questions for their own communities — and it shows Bhaiya's openness to practical suggestions fr om the sangat.
Exchange 2 — On the Repair & Maintenance Fund

Devotee: Bhaiya, hamare Jain dharm mein jitne bhi mandir hote hain, hum log hi maintain karte hain. Usme sabse pehla fund rehta hai sarv sadharan fund — woh repair and maintenance fund mein jaata hai poore mandir ka. Repair and maintenance fund khada karna bahut zaroori hai. Bhaiya: Baat toh sahi keh rahe hain aap, galat nahi keh rahe. Chaliye, main aapko saaf-saaf bata deta hoon — abhi humara yeh rehta hai ki hum Mahotsav ke liye paisa ikattha karte hain aur jitna bhi hota hai woh Baba ke charano mein bhog samarpit karne ki vyavastha mein jaata hai. Dheere-dheere hum jo bhi hai woh kar lenge — itna hume aata nahi hai par dheere-dheere hum usko kar lenge.

Why this is her e: A genuinely new practical governance discussion — Bhaiya publicly and transpar ently agr eeing to build financial infrastructur e the community has been informally asking about, in his own wor ds.
Exchange 3 — Why Bhaiya Never Asks for Money

Devotee: Bhaiya, ek suggestion tha — maangein kisse? Bhaiya: Jagat ke pita Jagdish se maangein. Aur ek baat aur bataata hoon — yaad rakh lena: jagat sath ho aur Jagdish rooth jaaye toh koi nahi bacha sakta. Aur jagat khilaf ho aur Jagdish sath ho toh aapka baal baanka nahi hota. Jab log aakar bolte hain toh main kehta hoon jai jai s ि ◌य ा र ा म — kyunki mujhe pata hai, mere Gurudev kehte hain duniya gol hai bachche, ghoom phir kar wahi tatva badalna hai. Bhaiya: Aap toh humare apne ho. Aapko toh diya jaata hai, aapse liya nahi jaata.

Why this is her e: A clean, quotable articulation of a cor e value in this teaching — that devotion is never transactional, and r equests should go to the divine, not to fellow devotees — likely to be r eferenced often by users asking about the community's appr oach to giving/r eceiving.
Exchange 4 — The App Wallet and Donation Suggestion

Devotee: Bhaiya, hamara jo Ashaeiynn ka app hai, usme agar ek wallet — payment wallet — aur donation ka kuch add kar dein... kai baar hamare paas paise arrange nahi ho paate ek time pe, toh hum apne wallet mein save karte rahein apne hisaab se. Devotee (continuing): Main yeh bol rahi hoon ki apni suvidha se — jitne bhi log Ashaeiynn se jude hain woh apne hisaab se thodi bahut madad kar sakte hain. Kisi ko bhi force nahi kiya jaayega, jisko karna hai woh kare. Bhaiya: Chalo ji, is baat ka poora dhyaan rakhenge aur zaroor is par kaarya karenge.

Why this is her e: A practical, actionable suggestion with Bhaiya's dir ect response — useful for any user wondering whether/how the community handles voluntary contributions, and shows the suggestion was hear d and taken seriously rather than dismissed.
